title: Spam filter: adversarial data augmentation significantly reduces an adaptive attacker

invariants.description: The stronger-effort attack must still evade the undefended filter (observed 27/93 = 29.0%).
Every adversarial message must satisfy every declared text-preservation constraint (re-validated from the stored text and edit script).
On the same messages, a NEW attack against the augmented model must succeed significantly less often (observed McNemar p = 1.7e-3).
Augmentation must remove at least 5 percentage points of adaptive success (observed 12.1 pp).
Augmentation must keep clean spam recall ≥ 88% (observed 117/128 = 91.4%).
Augmentation must keep the clean ham false-positive rate ≤ 1% (observed 5/904 = 0.55%).

rationale: Adversarial examples are generated from TRAINING spam only (300 messages, undefended model) and added with label spam; the held-out test messages are never seen during training.
